task: Turn web pages into clean Markdown with a self-hosted copy
packaging_note: Upstream's docker-compose.yaml with its published multi-arch images pinned by digest instead of 20-minute source builds; the API image was published by upstream CI five minutes after this commit and carries no revision label

access.why: It crawls the pages you give it, so its services reach the web.

inputs.what: one URL per line; blank lines and # comments are ignored

outputs.what: one Markdown file per URL, named from the URL without its scheme

known_issues: Upstream starts five queue workers of about 320 MB each, so its published API image idles at its 2.5 GB cap and is killed (exit 137) by the first scrape; NUQ_WORKER_COUNT=1 serves one user at about 1.4 GB. The stack's limits add up to 4.3 GB; it uses about 2 GB
The Docker Desktop VM failed to resolve some hosts until the API and browser services were given public DNS servers
No keys or accounts: authentication is off and the LLM extraction features are left unset
The API listens on a random 127.0.0.1 port (docker compose -f recipe/compose.yaml port api 3002); the task service calls it from inside the stack
The images total about 4.6 GB; on a slow connection the first start takes over ten minutes, nearly all of it downloading

Upstream's RabbitMQ health check runs as root and, when it runs before the server, writes an Erlang cookie the server cannot read, so the queue never starts; here the queue runs as its own user, and the queue and its database get two minutes to start on a busy machine
